races.name: Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Forever Endless
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's 3yo has shown modest form (two 5ths at Goodwood), and while a natural hold-up horse, is pushed forward on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded with closers; going is fine but find a step up in performance needed.

runners_data.name: Hope And Joy
runners_data.note: 289 days off the track is a significant concern, and a 10th on debut over 6f on soft ground offers little confidence; the headgear (p) is a new addition that hints connections are trying to spark improvement after a long absence.

runners_data.name: Oddjob
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed 3yo for Ed Walker (T14: 5/33), a yard in decent form; running style is unknown, going suitability is unknown — pure wildcard but Walker's juveniles and lightly raced types are worth respecting on debut.

runners_data.name: Asuka
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4yo who won on debut at Goodwood over 6f on good ground back in 2023 — this is a 697-day absence, which is the defining concern; the step to 7f on AW is unproven, and Billy Loughnane's booking is the main positive.

runners_data.name: Rua Mor
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a dismal recent record — five runs without a win or place in current form, all at 8f+ or staying trips; dropping to 7f on AW is a new angle but the consistent finishing position of 5th or worse is hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Bond
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Derek Shaw (T14: 0/1), a yard with limited recent strike rate; style and going suitability entirely unknown, making this a genuine wildcard with minimal form angles to assess.

runners_data.name: Rogue Invincible
runners_data.note: Shaped with promise when runner-up over this exact course and trip (7f, STA) and the style-fit is good for tracking a lone front-runner; Luke Morris is experienced around here and the return to a surface where it placed is the key positive.

runners_data.name: Tyrant Gg
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with a solid AW record (placed both starts on standard, including 2nd over 7f STA) and drawn in stall one; the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges it may be deployed more prominently than its natural role but Murphy's judgement from the front is the race's central tactical factor.

runners_data.name: Garth Spirit
runners_data.note: Debut 3yo for Robbie Llewellyn (T14: 0/0 — no recent runners), which makes form reading impossible; the lower weight (125lbs) is a minor positive but with no data on style, going or trip, this is firmly speculative.

runners_data.name: Tago Mago
runners_data.note: Sam England's 3yo has a directly relevant placed run (3rd, 7f, STA) which is an obvious positive; the hold-up style means relying on the pace collapsing, and the drop back from a poor recent effort (8th at Goodwood) needs explaining, but the course-and-distance form is genuine.

races.paceDynamic: Tyrant Gg is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to pressure from the outset, Oisin Murphy can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Wolverhampton's flat 7f Polytrack. Rogue Invincible and Asuka are the primary prominent types who will look to sit just off the leader, likely forming a small cluster in the early stages, but neither has the profile to blow Tyrant Gg away. The field contains more hold-up horses than the track map can naturally accommodate at the rear — Forever Endless is a genuine hold-up operator pushed into a midfield position on the map, meaning closers will be competing for limited late ground and those at the very back may lack the clear run they need. This race shape — a lone, unhurried pace-setter, a compact midfield, and cramped late closers — strongly favours prominent racers who can track Tyrant Gg and pounce inside the final furlong without needing a long run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tyrant Gg Leads Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Tyrant Gg is allowed to bowl along in front uncontested and sets a measured, even tempo.
scenarios.body: Murphy controls the fractions from stall one, the field settles into a compact bunch behind, and Tyrant Gg's proven ability on this surface (2/2 on standard AW) sees it quicken clear late; prominent trackers Rogue Invincible and Asuka are best placed to capitalise if it weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tyrant Gg fades in the final furlong after setting a brisk early pace and the prominent trackers overhaul it.
scenarios.body: Rogue Invincible or Asuka, having stalked the leader throughout, inherit the lead inside the final 1.5f and hold on as the closers arrive too late; this suits horses with a prominent racing pattern and recent AW experience.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the front rank ties up, allowing a well-positioned midfield horse to swoop.
scenarios.body: Tago Mago has placed on this exact track and trip (3rd, 7f, STA) and could exploit a collapsing pace; Forever Endless, though a true hold-up type racing out of its natural position, also carries claims if traffic opens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Wildcard Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three unraced or lightly raced unknowns (Oddjob, Cosmic Bond, Garth Spirit) produces an eye-catching debut performance.
scenarios.body: Unquantifiable ability means Oddjob or Garth Spirit could bolt up on debut with no exposed form for rivals to assess; trainer Ed Walker (T14: 5/33) gives Oddjob the most credible angle here.

watchPoints.text: Tyrant Gg's draw in stall one hands Oisin Murphy a free lead — watch whether any runner challenges for the early position in the first furlong, as uncontested fractions will strongly favour the front-runner.
Hope And Joy returns after 289 days off and debuts a hood (p) — a horse coming back cold after nearly a year with new headgear can show erratic early pace and may unsettle the field's initial shape.

Rua Mor has run at 16f twice in recent starts and drops dramatically in trip to 7f — watch for it being left behind early if the pace is lively, which would confirm it as a non-runner in practical terms for pace purposes.

Asuka has been absent 697 days — watch the market move and paddock closely, as any significant support would suggest connections have done serious homework ahead of what looks like a straightforward race-fit assignment.
Oddjob, Cosmic Bond and Garth Spirit are all debut runners — if two or more break sharply, the unchallenged pace-setter narrative around Tyrant Gg could be disrupted unexpectedly in the early stages.

races.name: Book Hotel & Conferencing At Wolverhampton Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Bishop's Glory
runners_data.note: Veteran of 5f Standard AW with a 1W5P sim-going record and visor applied; holds solid recent form (3rd, 5th) and trainer Ramsden runs two here — true hold-up horse that the redistribution has placed in midfield, where it will need a clean run to show its best.

runners_data.name: Chiedozie
runners_data.note: McEntee yard in quiet form (0/4 T14) and this five-year-old has finished no better than 3rd in 15 sim-going runs, but carries a hood and tongue-tie, suggesting connections are trying to get more from him; naturally sits at the rear and will need the pace to collapse for his late effort to matter.

runners_data.name: Baileys Ontherocks
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll in strong form (9/51 T14) and this three-year-old showed a hint of ability when 6th on debut, but an OR of 47 with no wins or places on Standard AW puts pressure on Billy Loughnane to manufacture a prominent position from a horse that idles at the back naturally.

runners_data.name: Dontwaryboutathing
runners_data.note: Flagged as a race-day fader and has just one sim-going run in the books (9th, 6f, STA); the OR of 44 and a trainer with a single runner in the 14-day window suggest limited confidence, and its 6-9-12 finishing positions at 6f make this 5f an optimistic cut in trip.

runners_data.name: Fuseboard
runners_data.note: Returned from a 56-day break and has five consecutive Standard AW runs without a win or place, all at 6f-8f — the drop to 5f is unexplored territory; trainer Banham has had one winner from five runners in the past fortnight, giving Joey Haynes something to work with if the pace sets up for closers.

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is the standout jockey booking in this field and the horse brings three places from five 5f sim-going runs; genuinely suited to this trip, and though it gravitates to hold-up tactics naturally, Murphy could push forward if the gates open slowly across the field.

runners_data.name: Rohini
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner (OR 41) and a claimer in the saddle (Taryn Langley, 5lb), but Ramsden has had two winners from 12 in the past fortnight; four consecutive defeats at 5f on varying going, with the best effort a 7th — needs everything to go right in what will be a chaotic sprint.

runners_data.name: Wondrous
runners_data.note: Michael Bell has two winners from 24 runners in the past fortnight, and this three-year-old is flagged as a fader — its best Standard AW effort was a 4th over 6f at Goodwood and it has gone backwards since; the blinkers are applied but finishing 9th-12th in recent races makes improvement hard to trust.

races.paceDynamic: This is a remarkable race in which every single runner is classified as a hold-up type, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner to set a true gallop over Wolverhampton's 5f. With no horse likely to commit fully from the gates, the early stages will be characterised by a scramble for position rather than a controlled lead, with the pace almost certainly ragged and uneven before runners begin to pick up entering the straight. Havin A Flyer, Baileys Ontherocks, and Bishop's Glory are the horses most likely to press forward from their redistributed midfield positions and manufacture something resembling a pace, though none are natural front-runners. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely settle at the rear — Havin A Flyer and Bishop's Glory, with the best recent form figures and sim-going records at this trip on Standard, are best placed to secure a competitive stalking position — and the overall shape strongly favours whoever can travel smoothly just off a slow-contested gallop and finish best in what will effectively be a sprint from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Scramble, Best Closer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the ragged early pace produces a compressed, stop-start gallop that sets up a flat-out dash for home from 2f out.
scenarios.body: With no true leader dictating tempo, the field will bunch and sprint from well inside the final two furlongs, rewarding the runner who travels most smoothly and produces the strongest late kick on Standard AW. A horse with proven 5f form on this surface and a jockey capable of timing a run through a tight field will hold the edge in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Front-Runner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one runner — most likely Havin A Flyer or Baileys Ontherocks — breaks sharply and decides to commit fully to the lead unchallenged.
scenarios.body: An uncontested leader over 5f on Standard AW Wolverhampton can dictate a pace that suits them perfectly and simply gallop rivals into submission, as the remaining field fails to coordinate a challenge until it is too late. The jockey on Havin A Flyer (Oisin Murphy) has the tactical nous to identify this opportunity and exploit it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Hold-Up Runs Late
scenarios.trigger: If two or more runners do press forward aggressively from the start, creating a genuine pace that burns them out by the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested early gallop over only 5f would be unusual given the field composition, but if it materialises it will leave the closing ground for horses who settle and come late — though all runners are true hold-up types, so the winner would be whoever covers ground most efficiently from midfield.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: All Meets Traffic, Fluke Outcome
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow and the sprint so chaotic that positional luck and draw dominate, overriding running style entirely.
scenarios.body: A wall of hold-up horses all arriving together in the final furlong creates maximum traffic and interference, meaning the horse in the clearest run — potentially dictated purely by stall draw — wins against the run of form. Wondrous and Dontwaryboutathing, flagged as faders, are unlikely beneficiaries even here.

watchPoints.text: Havin A Flyer — Oisin Murphy's presence is the key jockey edge in this race; watch for him to steal a march early and convert a no-pace scenario into a wire-to-wire lead before the field can organise.

Bishop's Glory and Rohini are trained by the same yard (Joey Ramsden) and running together — watch for a potential team tactic, with one pacemaking for the other, which could entirely reshape the expected slow pace.

Baileys Ontherocks has Tony Carroll's strong stable form behind it (9/51 T14) and Billy Loughnane could push forward aggressively in the absence of a true front-runner — any early move by this horse would instantly change the pace shape.

Dontwaryboutathing and Wondrous are both flagged as faders — if both drift back in the closing stages as expected, traffic congestion in the final furlong becomes a genuine risk for horses caught behind them.

The entire field is classified hold-up, meaning stall draw and early-break luck may carry more influence than normal — watch for any runner that gets a clean early jump to be unexpectedly prominent and difficult to catch.

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Standard AW 21 days ago for David Evans and Rossa Ryan but is a genuine hold-up type shuffled to a midfield map position; drops back in trip here and the race shape is unlikely to generate the searching pace this horse needs to produce its best finish.

runners_data.name: The Hare Rail
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with useful placed form including a 2nd at 8f on Standard AW recently; Owen Lewis (5lb claimer) takes off weight, and the horse has shown enough on this surface to be a player if given a smooth run from a stalking position.

runners_data.name: Cephalus
runners_data.note: A veteran of Standard AW at 7yo with a healthy 13 runs on similar going, this natural rear-runner has been pushed to the midfield map because the field is saturated with hold-up types; blinkers fitted and Joey Haynes rides, but 48 days off the track adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Auburn Avenue
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner who will lead from the gate and control the tempo; John & Rhys Flint have modest 14-day strike rate, limited sim-going form suggests this surface may not be wholly ideal, yet the positional advantage of an uncontested lead is a major asset at 1m½f.

runners_data.name: American State
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 4yo by handicap standards with two wins on Standard AW and a 135lb weight burden; Stevie Donohoe for Ivan Furtado's yard, which shows form with 4 winners from 28 in 14 days, and a hold-up tag that should find a comfortable position tracking the pace in this shape.

runners_data.name: Pursuit Of Truth
runners_data.note: Off 132 days, which is a significant fitness flag, but has a win over 10f on Standard AW and Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride; tongue-tie fitted and the step back from 11f to 1m½f (10f) looks potentially fine, though the layoff must be respected.

runners_data.name: Reds And Wolves
runners_data.note: Style listed as unknown, so positional behaviour is genuinely uncertain; Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey booking for Hugo Palmer's yard, and three runs at 7f on Standard AW suggest this trip up to 1m½f may be a stretch, though Palmer's 14-day figures are strong at 4/40.

runners_data.name: Kit Gabriel
runners_data.note: Has a creditable placed record including three 3rds in recent 7f Standard AW runs; Tyler Heard rides the 7yo, who maps to hold-up position but has placed form suggesting he can finish well in the right shape — a clean run from midfield could see him feature.

runners_data.name: Symphony's Song
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 4yo with only three career runs showing two respectable 4ths; a natural hold-up horse redeployed to midfield on the map given the field's configuration, and Luke Morris is a capable partner, but limited form makes confidence hard to establish.

runners_data.name: R P Mcmurphy
runners_data.note: Good recent form including a win and multiple 3rds on Standard AW at 8f for Michael Appleby; 144 days off the track is a concern, but the horse carries a hood and clearly has an affinity with this surface — Appleby's yard brings horses back fit and this deserves respect if fit.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago and returns quickly, which raises a freshness concern; visor worn and Billy Loughnane is a top pilot, but five consecutive finishes outside the frame at 6th or worse and a natural rear-running style squeezed to midfield on the map make this a difficult case.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 8yo carries the lowest weight (119lbs) with 7lb claimer Matthew Lloyd Slater; ran 12 days ago and showed a win on Standard AW at 7f in recent history, with strong sim-going figures, though age and a redistribution away from natural hold-up territory limits optimism.

races.paceDynamic: Auburn Avenue is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead from the outset on Standard Wolverhampton AW over 1m½f, setting a controlled, sustainable tempo with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead. The large hold-up contingent — eleven of twelve runners are natural rear or midfield types — means the field will be strung out behind with limited early pressure on the pace, creating a genuine advantage for those racing in touch rather than being asked to make up ground from a true hold-up position. Runners redistributed to the midfield map — Eagle Day, Cephalus, Symphony's Song, R P Mcmurphy, Bajan Bandit, and River Wharfe — are genuine hold-up horses by nature, and with too many of them to slot to the rear, several will race awkwardly out of role with compromised finishes. The tactical verdict is clear: horses able to race prominently or in a close stalking position behind Auburn Avenue are best placed, as the measured gallop will not generate the searching pace that true closers need to overhaul leaders from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Auburn Avenue Controls Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Auburn Avenue bowls along uncontested and the hold-up horses fail to generate enough pace to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Auburn Avenue dictates from the front at a comfortable tempo, and any rival racing prominently off her shoulder sits in the best position entering the straight; with no genuine pace-pressure the race becomes a test of class and stamina in the final two furlongs rather than a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned just off Auburn Avenue's shoulder travels well throughout and hits the front in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The controlled early fractions allow a close-tracking runner to conserve energy and deliver a decisive challenge as Auburn Avenue ties up; this suits a horse with decent form on Standard AW surfaces who can be placed handily.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and horses racing in the middle of the pack mount a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: A more honest gallop than expected could string the field out and allow a quality midfield mover to pick off tiring rivals; this shape depends partly on redistributed hold-up horses finding an unobstructed run, which is inherently uncertain given their forced positional compromise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns genuinely strong in the second half of the race and the backmarkers get an unimpeded run.
scenarios.body: True hold-up types left at the rear would need a meaningful tempo and clear daylight in the straight to finish past rivals; given only one confirmed front-runner and the field's natural bunching, the conditions for a vintage late swooper are unlikely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Auburn Avenue's uncontested lead is the defining shape-setter — watch whether any rival breaks fast enough from the gates to push her in the early stages, which would fundamentally alter the pace dynamic.

R P Mcmurphy and Pursuit Of Truth both return from lengthy absences (144 days and 132 days respectively) — if either is short of peak fitness their chance is materially reduced regardless of form profile.

Six horses are redistributed from true hold-up positions to the midfield map — watch the early running order to see which of Eagle Day, Cephalus, Symphony's Song, R P Mcmurphy, Bajan Bandit, and River Wharfe actually settles where, as traffic problems in the straight are a real risk.
Bajan Bandit runs for the second time in three days — monitor market moves for any sign of stable confidence, but quick back-up combined with out-of-role positioning on the map suggests caution.

Oisin Murphy's booking for Reds And Wolves stands out in an otherwise modest jockey line-up — watch whether the market reacts, given the unknown running style and the step up in trip from repeated 7f runs.

races.name: Cavani Sartorial Classified Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Rogue Soldier
runners_data.note: Trainer Max Young is 0/2 in the 14-day window and the horse carries the burden of 166 days off the track; genuinely races as a hold-up type but will find itself shuffled into midfield in this field, which blunts its already modest record at this course and trip.

runners_data.name: Stacey Racey
runners_data.note: 119 days absent is a significant concern and Keiran Burke's yard is running at 2/7 short-term; a natural rear-of-field operator who will occupy a midfield slot by necessity here, having placed four times without winning at similar class.

runners_data.name: Blue Jammin
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick runners have gone 0/16 in the 14-day window — a stark stat to note before anything else; this three-year-old also flags a tendency to fade late and its similar-going record of 2/10 at AW is thin, so the enforced midfield berth compounds already difficult conditions.

runners_data.name: First Encounter
runners_data.note: The key horse tactically — Luke Morris can set his own rhythm unchallenged, the yard is 2/7 in the 14-day window, and this horse has won and placed repeatedly at Wolverhampton on standard; the one-off nature of this lead role is its primary asset today.

runners_data.name: Ignition
runners_data.note: Thomas Faulkner sends this one out 1/7 in the 14-day window which provides mild encouragement; a genuine hold-up horse in nature, it will be packaged into midfield with the others, and its trip form is solid over 10f on standard, though it has yet to win.

runners_data.name: Masqool
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll operates at 10/45 short-term — a busy and respectable yard — and Masqool has shown consistent placed form over 10f including multiple good-ground thirds; races naturally off the pace but is one of the most credible challengers to First Encounter if it can track prominently.

runners_data.name: Gloriola
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead is 2/12 in the 14-day window and this three-year-old has placed at Wolverhampton over 8f on standard, which is directly relevant course form; a natural hold-up type who could benefit from sitting second or third should the pace prove generous.

runners_data.name: Jean's Boy
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's charge is 2/33 in the 14-day window and this is only a three-run career for a lightly-raced three-year-old; a genuine closer who also flags a tendency to fade at the finish — both the out-of-role position and the finishing-fade flag are meaningful negatives here.

runners_data.name: Nautical Sky
runners_data.note: James Ferguson is 1/4 in the 14-day window and Nautical Sky has placed at Wolverhampton over 8f on standard, showing it handles the track; races as a hold-up type but has the strongest similarity-going placed record of the closers, making it the most interesting of those chasing home.

races.paceDynamic: First Encounter is the lone confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, Luke Morris will be able to dictate a controlled, even gallop throughout the 1m½f Wolverhampton circuit. The bulk of the field are true hold-up types — Rogue Soldier, Stacey Racey, Blue Jammin, Ignition, Masqool, Gloriola, Jean's Boy and Nautical Sky all prefer to race off the pace, meaning First Encounter faces zero pressure and can set whatever fractions suit. With a sustainable, uncontested lead on a track that notoriously favours prominent racers who can preserve energy through the bends, this race shape emphatically suits a horse who can roll along in front and quicken clear rather than those hunting them down late. Several redistributed hold-up types — particularly Rogue Soldier, Stacey Racey and Blue Jammin — are genuine closers who cannot access their natural rear position in this compressed, largely pace-less field and will be squeezed into midfield roles that suit none of them cleanly, further reducing the chance of a late sweeping finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: First Encounter Dictates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If First Encounter gets a clean break and is allowed to roll into an uncontested lead at a comfortable gallop.
scenarios.body: Morris controls tempo through the first bend unchallenged, conserving First Encounter throughout and kicking for home turning in — on this track, with no rival close enough to apply pressure, that profile is very hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pegs Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If First Encounter's gallop is slightly more generous than ideal and a horse tracking just off the pace moves smoothly to challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse in second or third position through the race will have the race run into their hands if the leader edges fractionally wide or fades in the final furlong; Masqool or Gloriola, each with placed form at similar trips, are best placed to capitalise from that chasing berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land A Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and the hold-up brigade, despite their compressed midfield positions, sprint home with purpose.
scenarios.body: This is a lower-probability shape because the horses best suited to it — Rogue Soldier, Stacey Racey, Blue Jammin — are all racing out of their natural role and will lack the clean passage a true late closer needs; only an unusually strong late kick from Nautical Sky or Stacey Racey makes this viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for midfield position causes a bunched, slowly-run contest that results in a sprint finish with several horses arriving together.
scenarios.body: A chaotic pace with multiple jockeys wide on the track trying to avoid trouble could neutralise First Encounter's structural advantage and hand the race to a horse that stumbles into a clear run; Nautical Sky's placed Wolverhampton form makes it the most obvious beneficiary of disorder.

watchPoints.text: First Encounter's draw and break are critical — if Luke Morris gets a clean, uncontested lead from the first stride, the race is likely over as a contest before it truly begins.
Blue Jammin has a confirmed fade-in-finish flag alongside an 0/16 trainer 14-day record — if prominent in the market, this combination makes it a horse to treat with considerable caution.

Jean's Boy also carries a fade-in-finish flag and is lightly raced over only three starts — watch whether Harry Vigors (5) can find a position that compensates, given the horse's natural late style is compromised by the field shape.

With Rogue Soldier returning from 166 days off, monitor its movement in the market late — a well-backed drift or shortening will be informative given the fitness question mark and out-of-role positioning.

Masqool and Gloriola are the two hold-up horses with the most plausible routes to a placing — watch which jockey commits earlier to track First Encounter, as the one who secures second or third on the rail turning in holds the best each-way claims.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Nutcracker
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Tony Carroll — sim-going figures show 0W2P in nine similar-going runs, suggesting placed rather than winning form; at 31 days fresh and stretching to 1m½f from recent 7-8f starts, the extra trip is a question.|

runners_data.name: Wingstar
runners_data.note: Michael Keady runner whose last four runs include poor efforts at 8-10f on Standard; a genuine deep hold-up type who will be pushed out of natural position in this traffic-heavy rear, limiting scope to express best form.|

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and has finished outside the places in every recent run, including poor efforts on Good and Standard; dropping to 3yo allowance helps marginally but in-running style forces her back into a crowded midfield that suits no one here.|

runners_data.name: Celebrating Ethel
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's seven-year-old has a course-distance win on Standard in her last five runs and a respectable 8/15 sim-going record; Myla Coppins claims 7lb and is likely to push forward into prominent ground, which is where this race will be won.|

runners_data.name: Kessaar Power
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's gelding has consistent placed form at 7-8f on Standard (1W2P in 15 runs) and is being held up by redistribution despite wanting to race prominently; Connor Planas will likely push forward early to claim a tracking position behind Knightmare.|

runners_data.name: Knightmare
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed pace-setter and clear tactical pivot of this field — David Evans sends him back just six days after his last run, and Billy Loughnane can dictate every yard at Wolverhampton's flat track; his 0W2P in eight sim-going runs suggests he places well but struggles to convert.|

runners_data.name: Churchill's Spirit
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's three-year-old blinkered today, with only four career starts and a poor sim-going record of 0W0P in two Standard runs; true hold-up nature means he must race out of role in this field, and the blinkers are a first-time variable to monitor.|

runners_data.name: King's Courtier
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and has a poor recent record including two finishes of 11th and 13th; the 3yo allowance helps on weight but form reads as a race-experience builder rather than a winning vehicle.|

runners_data.name: Three Builders
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick's three-year-old wears headgear (hood) and has no Standard going experience in last five — all runs on Good or Soft; a trip step-up and surface switch make this a speculative entry rather than a confident play.|

races.paceDynamic: Knightmare is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field over Wolverhampton's 1m½f Tapeta trip, and with no genuine rival to push them for the lead, Billy Loughnane should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. The remainder of the field is stacked with hold-up types — Kessaar Power, Churchill's Spirit, Celebrating Ethel, Wingstar and others — who will be forced to race closer to the pace than their natural style dictates simply because there is no mid-race cavalry charge to sit behind. This field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the map can naturally accommodate at the rear; Knightmare is near-certain to secure the lead, and the most likely runners to push into prominent positions behind are Kessaar Power and Celebrating Ethel given their prior placements and handlers' records. A steady, front-running tempo managed by Knightmare firmly favours horses that can track within two to three lengths of the lead and quicken from a prominent pitch, as deep closers will find the pace insufficient to generate the late sprint they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Knightmare Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Knightmare is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead at a measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Loughnane sets fractions that never truly stretch the field, meaning the race becomes a test of finishing kick from a compact group rather than stamina — Knightmare's consistency in placing from the front is a significant asset here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse repositions prominently behind Knightmare and outkicks them in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The steady tempo invites horses that can travel close to the pace without burning fuel early, and a prominent-tracking run sets up a clean delivery into the straight; Celebrating Ethel's course-distance win and Kessaar Power's market presence both align with this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Falters, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Knightmare goes too hard early or ties up in the closing stages, opening the door for closers.
scenarios.body: A collapse in the leader's gallop over this trip is not impossible given Knightmare's modest stamina profile at 1m½f, and any falter benefits the deepest-sitting hold-up runners; however, so many of those types are racing out of their natural position that a genuine late flourish is structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Crowded Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses ignore their natural hold-up roles and contest for prominent ground, creating a muddled pace scenario.
scenarios.body: With seven horses compressed into midfield and only one natural leader, positional friction in the early stages could disrupt the rhythm and produce an untidy race that scrambles the form; this shape suits horses that handle traffic and have tactical versatility.

watchPoints.text: Knightmare (Billy Loughnane) — watch for whether they get an uncontested lead from the off; if anything rushes them in the first two furlongs, the entire pace scenario shifts.|

Celebrating Ethel and Kessaar Power — both genuine hold-up types likely to push forward early; if they clash for the same prominent slot behind Knightmare, expect traffic issues and a disrupted race shape inside the final three furlongs.|

Churchill's Spirit wears blinkers for the first time — first-time headgear at Wolverhampton can produce an unpredictable jump-away or exaggerated early effort that could compress the field from the back.|
Three Builders has no Tapeta/Standard going experience in recent form — monitor market moves for this runner as any drifting suggests connections are also uncertain about the surface switch.|

races.name: Follow @attheraces On X Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: The Fixer
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer at 5f-6f on AW Standard, boasting a win and three places from 15 similar-going runs; Kieran O'Neill has to ride cold from the back of what is a pace-light field, which is a real tactical challenge here.

runners_data.name: Crown Dreams
runners_data.note: Returns from 901 days off the track for Robert Cowell — that layoff is the dominant factor; a natural rear-runner whose true style has been pushed forward on the map, and the lengthy absence overrides any positional consideration.

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides a horse fresh off a 6-day turnaround, with form showing placed efforts at 5f-6f on AW Standard; positioned naturally toward the rear but the light pace may allow a forward-creeping move from this hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Tomarlo
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has Sean D Bowen in the saddle for Ollie Sangster, who is in decent form (T14: 4/24); beaten by just two-and-a-half lengths in a placed effort at 5f on Soft last time, but the natural rear-running style is compromised by the lack of pace in this race.

runners_data.name: Lifeguard
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Mark Loughnane's yard ridden by Billy Loughnane, kept in the family; no wins in six starts and a 23-day break, with all recent form showing mid-division finishes — going form is fine but consistency is the concern.

runners_data.name: Unique Procedure
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with only three career runs, all on turf Soft or Good; Julia & Shelley Birkett's charge is lightly raced and unexposed but the hold-up style means the lack of a strong pace is an obstacle to showing best.

runners_data.name: Mintana
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed pace-setter, with a win and four places from 11 runs on AW Standard and a course win over 7f; the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is technically a prominent horse rather than a pure leader, but in this company she will get to the front comfortably and dictate on her own terms.

runners_data.name: Maury
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on AW Standard two runs back for Craig Benton; back from 15 days off and a natural hold-up performer pushed toward the midfield by the map redistribution — the longer trips in her recent history (7f-8f) raise a mild stamina concern on a sharp 6f.

runners_data.name: Conquest Of Power
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has finished placed in 5 of 13 AW Standard runs including two wins, giving him the strongest course-and-distance credentials in the field after Mintana; 65 days off for Mark Usher and a hold-up style repositioned closer on the map, but his AW record gives him a realistic each-way profile.

runners_data.name: No News
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed over 6f on AW Standard before for J R Jenkins; 47 days off and a natural closer whose hold-up tendencies have been mapped forward — the STA going form (8 runs) suggests he handles the surface, though wins are elusive.

runners_data.name: Power Cut
runners_data.note: Three-year-old at the bottom of the weights for Chelsea Banham, 70 days since last seen; all four runs came on AW Standard and all four finished in 5th-6th, showing a consistent but uninspiring level — a hold-up type with no wins and no pace to chase.

races.paceDynamic: Mintana is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap at Wolverhampton and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge for the lead, she should enjoy a soft, uncontested passage from the front on Standard AW ground. The rest of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up or midfield in profile, meaning the early gallop is likely to be controlled and honest rather than scorching — a pace that will keep the race together rather than string it out. This shape heavily favours horses who can race prominently just behind Mintana and pounce in the straight, rather than true closers who need a fast tempo to close into. The field holds more hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear — Crown Dreams, Tomarlo, Unique Procedure, Maury, Conquest Of Power, No News and Power Cut have all been redistributed forward on the map; of these, Conquest Of Power and No News have the AW form to suggest they may find a position closer than their natural style, but Mintana remains the likeliest to dictate throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mintana Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mintana is allowed to stride clear from the gate and control a steady-to-honest pace with no rival pressing her.
scenarios.body: Mintana rolls along uncontested on the front end, setting a sustainable gallop that suits her stamina on 7f-form, and the lack of early pressure means she is still travelling within herself turning for home; her six wins on AW Standard and strong place record make her the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough that the horses who manage to find a prominent position from the midfield pack overhaul Mintana in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up types who secure a handy position — most likely Conquest Of Power or No News given their AW course form — close to within striking range and use the Standard surface to finish powerfully; The Fixer, with a win and three places over the course and distance on similar going, could also land this shape from further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Mintana's steady fractions cause the whole pack to bunch and a prominent tracker kicks clear with her from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A horse like Fancy Dancer or Lifeguard, sitting just off the pace and conserving energy through a moderate gallop, finds a clear run in the straight and outstays the leader; the absence of early pressure means the front two are clear of the hold-up horses still struggling to find room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If Mintana sets a surprisingly strong gallop that burns off the midfield pack and one true hold-up type catches them all close home.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the majority of closers have been redistributed and are not operating in their natural role, reducing their finishing effectiveness; only The Fixer — a genuine hold-up performer with course-and-distance credibility — carries real claims in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Mintana must be watched in the stalls and at the break — if she misses the kick, the entire race shape collapses as there is no other horse to set any meaningful gallop.

Conquest Of Power's 65-day layoff is a flag, but his 13 AW Standard runs give him the most credible course form among the closers — watch whether Rhys Clutterbuck places him prominently to offset the hold-up label.
The heavy redistribution of hold-up types risks a messy, bunched mid-race scenario where several horses try to claim the same ground turning in — traffic incidents are a real risk in the straight.
Crown Dreams has not raced in 901 days; even if she possesses residual ability, the extreme layoff for a six-year-old warrants major caution before putting weight on her chance.
Power Cut's consistent 5th-6th finishes at 5f-6f on AW Standard suggest a horse that runs to a ceiling — useful pace context as a benchmark but unlikely to significantly improve on that level today.

races.name: Follow AtTheRaces On X Handicap

runners_data.name: Amaysmont
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up runner trained by Kevin & Lauren Frost, Rossa Ryan booked; only 0W2P on similar going from 15 runs but showed a placed effort two weeks ago over 6f on Standard, and his experience in messy sprint finishes keeps him relevant.|

runners_data.name: Walking On Clouds
runners_data.note: Banham's seven-year-old has the most compelling Standard-going record in this field (14/15, 2W3P), Joey Haynes takes the ride; runs with a hood and is proven over this course and distance, making him the most course-qualified horse in the race.|

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's four-year-old wears a hood and is genuinely a hold-up horse — pushed into a midfield mapping here because the rear is overcrowded, but its true finishing style may be compromised in a race where everyone wants to come late; 0W3P on Standard is worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Hellcat
runners_data.note: Ross Burdon's three-year-old carries a specific warning flag for fading in the finish, which is a critical liability in a race that will almost certainly be decided by a late sprint; only 1/7 on similar going and the trainer's T14 strike rate of 2/3 does not offset the finishing concern.|

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Micky Fenton's three-year-old, Grace McEntee up, ran just eight days ago and showed 0W3P on similar going; a genuine hold-up type whose natural role is pushed forward by the crowded rear — her trip and going profile are acceptable but style-fit concerns at 0.91 are real.|

runners_data.name: Miss Magic Dragon
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave rides this three-year-old for D Donovan; won once on Good ground at 6f but has 0W0P on Standard and the style-fit score of 0.92 reflects that her true hold-up role is compromised by redistribution — 32 days since last run adds a fitness query.|

runners_data.name: Dr Ali
runners_data.note: Jenkins' four-year-old has a strong sim-going record (13/15, 2W4P on Standard) and wears a hood; Jonny Peate rides and the horse ran only nine days ago, suggesting sharpness — prior wins on 6f Standard make this one of the more qualified hold-up types in the field despite redistribution.|

runners_data.name: Jake Loves Laura
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's four-year-old returns from 129 days off, which is the most significant layoff in this field and a substantial concern; Gina Mangan rides and the horse's solid Standard record (13/15, 0W4P) is partly undermined by the long absence and redistribution out of its true hold-up position.|

runners_data.name: Red Walls
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson's eight-year-old returns after 162 days — the longest absence in the race — and the trainer has no T14 runners logged; last run was a placing on Standard over 6f but the extended layoff and redistribution from a genuine hold-up style are compounding risks.|

runners_data.name: Dreamcrafter
runners_data.note: Craig Benton's four-year-old has 0W0P on Standard from three runs and Georgia Dobie takes the ride; the 36-day break is manageable but the complete absence of a placed finish on Standard going, combined with a style-fit of 0.90 racing out of true hold-up role, makes this the least likely beneficiary of the probable sprint finish.|

races.paceDynamic: This is a ten-runner 6f handicap at Wolverhampton with no confirmed front-runner in the field — every single runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning the race will drift into a slow-crawl early before exploding into a wall-to-wall sprint from around the two-furlong pole. Without anyone willing to commit to the lead, the pace will be artificially compressed, the field bunching together and creating a messy, muddling contest where position in the straight matters more than trajectory through the race. The entire field holds more natural hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear — Walking On Clouds, Dr Ali and Amaysmont are arguably best-placed to slot into a forward berth if the early tempo vacuum forces horses to push up, but none are confirmed pace-makers. In this shape, horses with the clearest form on Standard AW surfaces, the sharpest finishing kick over 6f, and the widest recent sim-going record on this track will hold the edge — the race favours those who can quicken sharply in a sprint finish rather than horses who need a true pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner commits to the lead and the field crawls into a mass sprint from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The absence of any front-runner means the pack races as one unit, compressing the field into a late dash where track position and a sharp, instantaneous kick become decisive. Horses with the strongest Standard AW form at Wolverhampton and proven finishing ability in these slow-tempo 6f contests will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: AW Course Specialists Strike
scenarios.trigger: If horses with the deepest Wolverhampton Standard form assert in the closing stages
scenarios.body: Walking On Clouds (14/15 sim-going record, 2W3P on Standard) and Dr Ali (13/15 sim-going, previous wins on Standard) hold the clearest credentials for this surface and will be hard to peg back when the sprint begins. Their AW familiarity and class at this level give them a tangible edge over rivals with limited Standard track exposure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Suits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of early tempo creates significant shuffling and scrimmaging that opens a gap for a lower-ranked runner
scenarios.body: With all ten runners vying for similar late positions and no horse dictating terms, traffic problems are inevitable and a resolute stayer-type who can find a clear run at the death could emerge. Miss Magic Dragon's one win came on Good ground but her redistribution to midfield here means she is unlikely to reproduce that form under these conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Dawdle Wastes Field
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that the race degenerates into a pure reaction-time sprint from the final furlong
scenarios.body: In a complete slow-burn contest the field converges so tightly that the result is almost arbitrary, decided by luck in running and the jockey who spots daylight earliest. Hellcat and Dreamcrafter carry significant concerns here — Hellcat has a noted fade in finish and Dreamcrafter has 0W0P on Standard, making both unlikely beneficiaries even if the shape theoretically suits their profile.

watchPoints.text: Walking On Clouds is the one runner with genuine Standard-AW form credentials (14/15 sim-going) and must be tracked from the moment the stalls open — if Joey Haynes can find a position without being blocked in the sprint, this horse is the one best-equipped to quicken.|

Red Walls and Jake Loves Laura both return from lay-offs of 162 and 129 days respectively — watch for signs of rustiness in the early stages; either could be caught flat-footed when the sprint ignites if ring-rust costs them a crucial stride.|

Hellcat carries a specific finish-fade flag and William Carver will need to nurse this horse carefully through the bunched early pace — if the race develops into a sustained 2f sprint rather than a short sharp burst, Hellcat's chance evaporates quickly.|

Dr Ali ran just nine days ago and has the best sim-going strike rate among the redistributed hold-up runners; watch whether Jonny Peate attempts to push forward early to compensate for the overcrowded rear — any forward move from this horse changes the race shape meaningfully.|

With every runner mapped as a hold-up type, monitor the first furlong for any horse that instinctively goes forward — even a modest break from Amaysmont or Walking On Clouds could create an uncontested lead and completely alter the race shape from the expected sprint-finish scenario.|

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 512 Handicap

runners_data.name: Havachoc
runners_data.note: Sole genuine front-runner here; Billy Loughnane in fine form and the Patrick Morris yard is 1/3 in the last fortnight — four-day turnaround suggests freshness, and the STYLE_FIT tag is a mild concern but is outweighed by the uncontested lead this field will gift it at 1m6f on Standard AW.|

runners_data.name: Kingston Sunflower
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's veteran nine-year-old returns from a 294-day break (25 runs this jockey partnership); five of its last five form runs are over 16f and it won at this trip on Good, so the distance is ideal — but the fitness question after a near-ten-month absence is the dominant issue here.|

runners_data.name: The Craftymaster
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's gelding won over this exact trip at Wolverhampton on Standard going (its most recent run), which is the standout course-and-distance credential in this field; Myla Coppins claims 7lb which helps the weight, and a nine-day turnaround suggests the stable is happy — natural hold-up style will require Havachoc to weaken.|

runners_data.name: V Power
runners_data.note: Zoe Lewis (7) takes the ride on this horse that has two wins from 14f on Standard AW going and shaped promisingly last time over the same surface; runs at the back of its field as a pure hold-up operator, so needs the pace to be genuine — the 39-day break is manageable.|

runners_data.name: Mick The Hat
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett sends Rossa Ryan north for a three-year-old who has not won in five starts and whose best effort was a third over 12f on Soft; by nature a hold-up horse, it has been mapped to midfield here because the field is stacked with closers — its redistribution limits the chance of finding its true running style, and it steps up markedly in distance.|

runners_data.name: Last Flight
runners_data.note: James Ferguson's lightly raced three-year-old has finished no better than fifth in four career starts, all at shorter trips than today's 1m6f, with three of those runs at 8-10f on Standard AW; a natural hold-up type displaced to midfield by this field's close configuration, and stepping up significantly in trip for the first time makes this a tough ask.|

races.paceDynamic: Havachoc is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m6f Wolverhampton handicap and should dictate from the gate at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over the Tapeta surface, having raced prominently throughout its recent form. Behind, the four hold-up horses — The Craftymaster, V Power, Mick The Hat, and Last Flight — will be funnelled into a rear-to-midfield pack, creating a compact, processional shape with little pressure on the leader. Kingston Sunflower profiles as a prominent type who may attempt to track Havachoc, but a 294-day absence is a significant concern for its ability to maintain that position late. With the gallop controlled by one horse and true hold-up specialists unable to run their natural race from deep, this race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the straight without needing a strong pace to run into — closers who depend on a true end-to-end gallop to deliver their best will be working against the grain of this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Havachoc Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Havachoc leads at a measured pace and is never seriously pressured, dictating the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Havachoc sets a comfortable, unforced gallop around the Wolverhampton oval and simply keeps finding enough in the straight with no rival able to run it down; Billy Loughnane can switch off the pace perfectly at 1m6f, a trip that suits. Prominent-to-patient profiles travelling within themselves just behind get the best tow into the race and are best placed to challenge, but the leader's control advantage is substantial.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Gets The Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stop Havachoc and a hold-up horse threads through in the straight.
scenarios.body: The Craftymaster has won at this course over this trip on Standard going and represents the most credentialed hold-up horse in the field to exploit a setup that gets faster late; V Power has also shown Wolverhampton AW form at 14f and could emerge from midfield. Both carry the caution that the race is unlikely to truly suit them with the pace as controlled as it appears, making this scenario dependent on something going tactically wrong for the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Long Absence Flyer
scenarios.trigger: If Kingston Sunflower, despite 294 days off, travels powerfully on a return to its favoured trip and grabs the race in the straight.
scenarios.body: Kingston Sunflower has five runs at 16f on its card including a course win, and the O'Brien yard has sent it out fit enough after a lengthy absence before; if the fitness is there it has the tactical position to benefit from tracking the leader. However, the extended layoff and moderate sim-going record make this a low-probability flyer rather than a structured threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Youth Upsets The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If either of the three-year-olds — Mick The Hat or Last Flight — improves past their modest recent form and picks off tiring older rivals late.
scenarios.body: Both are lightly framed youngsters mapped away from their natural hold-up positions and carry no wins between them over any course or going; Last Flight's four-race form string shows all finishes of fifth or worse, while Mick The Hat has yet to win. A dramatic step up in form is required from either, and their redistribution away from the rear makes their natural late-run harder to execute.

watchPoints.text: Havachoc (Loughnane) jumps cleanly and reaches the lead — if unchallenged by the bend the race may be effectively over by the home straight, so watch its position at the start closely.

Kingston Sunflower's jumping and early energy in the first furlong will reveal how fit it is after 294 days off; if it rushes up aggressively it may be surprisingly forward, but if it travels flat it is effectively out of the race.

The Craftymaster is the only runner with a confirmed course-and-distance win on this exact going, and if it appears to be travelling easily entering the back straight it could mount a credible late challenge — watch its position turning for home.

Mick The Hat and Last Flight are both mapped away from their natural hold-up berths; if either appears keen or out of position early, their ability to produce their typical late run will be further compromised and they can be discounted.
